ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory automated and manual screening against French Tracfin/FIU PEP lists, OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU consolidated sanctions list, and domestic French sanctions lists in full compliance with AML/CFT regulations

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory use of French language and Latin script; foreign names must be transliterated into French where required by local naming conventions
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Reserved professional terms including 'banque', 'assurance', 'financement', 'paiement', 'carte virtuelle', 'émetteur de moyens de paiement' without prior ministerial or ACPR authorization; names that could mislead the public or imply public authority status
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal rejection by Infogreffe, the applicant must file an administrative appeal with the Minister of the Economy within two months of notification; failure to appeal within the deadline precludes subsequent judicial review before the administrative courts

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for standard SARL formation provided the registered office satisfies legal address requirements (including reception of mail and documents); however, for high-risk activities such as corporate virtual card issuing requiring payment institution license, a physical office may be mandated by the ACPR or Banque de France
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (under 10%) during pre-incorporation stage; rises to moderate (25-40%) upon application for banking or e-money institution license involving on-site verification by regulatory authorities

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title III, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL); Articles L.210-2, R.123-31 et seq. (registration); French Monetary and Financial Code, Articles L.522-1 et seq. and L.522-11-1 (payment institution authorisation for the corporate virtual-card issuing activity).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) of the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office, acting through the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs de la Société à Responsabilité Limitée (Articles of Association) executed by all shareholders, accompanied by the electronic creation declaration (Déclaration de création d'entreprise) transmitted to the Greffe via the Guichet Unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to a French SARL (Code de commerce, Article L.223-2); however, the payment-institution activity requires initial own funds of at least EUR 125,000 under Article L.522-11-1 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. Before registration, at least 20% of cash capital contributions, and here the full EUR 125,000, must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) with a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the balance, if any, must be released within five years, and for ACPR licensing purposes the full amount must remain available.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The subscribers extend the corporate foundation as follows: (1) adoption of the Articles of Association of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée, whose corporate name and registered office in France are set out therein; (2) subscription in full of the share capital of EUR 125,000, split into equal parts sociales, and approval of the blocked escrow deposit with the chosen depository bank until official registration; (3) appointment of [Name Surname] as Gérant for the Company's duration, with full powers of management and representation toward third parties; (4) authorization given to the Gérant to publish the mandatory legal notice, file the incorporation dossier via the Guichet Unique, procure the Kbis, and initiate the ACPR payment-institution license application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts) and Capital Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All founding shareholders acting jointly; optional notary public (acte notarié) where in-kind property contributions are made
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the French-law statuts of the SARL in accordance with Articles L.223-1 and L.223-7 of the French Commercial Code, specifying the corporate name, corporate purpose (limited to issuing corporate virtual cards and spend-management payment services), duration (maximum 99 years), registered office, share capital divided into equal parts sociales, number and nominal value of shares, appointment of the first Gérant, and the shareholding and beneficial-ownership breakdown. Have each founder sign the statuts in person or by duly authorized power of attorney. Verify that no contribution in industry (know-how) is counted toward share capital; for any in-kind contribution, obtain a valuation report from the contribution auditor (commissaire aux apports) if the value of a contribution exceeds EUR 30,000 or the aggregate value exceeds 50% of the share capital, unless the exemption in Article L.223-9 C. com. applies.
required_dossiers: Draft and executed copies of the statuts
Identity documents (passport or national ID) of each natural-person shareholder
Power of attorney for any signatory acting by representation
Valuation report of the in-kind contribution auditor (commissaire aux apports), if applicable
Criminal-record extract (bulletin n°3) of the proposed Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry's legality review identifies a null or non-compliant clause, adopt a rectifying resolution (avenant) signed by all shareholders and remove the offending provision before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Escrow Deposit of Share Capital and Issuance of the Bank Attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary pre-registration account in the Company's name (SARL en formation) and deposit at least 20% of the cash capital contributions, and, in this regulated scenario, deposit the full EUR 125,000 initial own funds required for the payment-institution licensing. Instruct the bank to issue the certificate of capital deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds) listing the depositor, the beneficiary company, the amount in euros, and the blocked-account status. The funds may be released to the Company's operational account only upon presentation of the Kbis extract after registration.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the executed statuts
AML/KYC file including beneficial-ownership documentation of each shareholder
Identity documents of the account signatories
Draft corporate bank account agreement
Power of attorney if the deposit is made through a corporate services provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account for AML or compliance reasons, commence the deposit procedure with an alternative licensed credit institution and re-issue the attestation in the exact legal name and with the exact capital amount stated in the statuts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Announcement in an Authorized Legal Notice Journal (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales authorized in the département of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit a formal notice containing the corporate name, the SARL legal form, share capital amount, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, and the identity of the Gérant to the licensed JAL. Verify that the notice is published before filing with the Guichet Unique and collect the attestation of publication (attestation de parution), including the JAL issue date.
required_dossiers: Completed legal announcement text
Extract of the approved statuts
Proof of payment of the publication fee
Identity of the Gérant for the notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is refused or contains an erroneous mention, publish a corrected version in a different authorized JAL and attach both the original refusal note and the corrected attestation to the filing dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Digital Filing of the Formation Dossier at the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by INPI and transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online application for the registration (immatriculation) of the legal entity in the Société à Responsabilité Limitée category. Attach all mandatory PDF documents, pay the greffe registration fee and taxes, and ensure the registered office justification matches the office that will appear on the Kbis. The Greffe deems the dossier complete upon electronic acknowledgment; the legal-entity SIREN/SIRET and Kbis are generated after validation by the registry judge.
required_dossiers: Scanned executed statuts
Bank certificate of blocked capital deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
Legal notice publication certificate (attestation de parution) from the JAL
Justification of the registered office (lease, domiciliation letter from the office landlord, or occupancy title)
Consent of the Gérant to the appointment (acte de nomination)
Identity document and criminal-record extract of the Gérant
Declaration of beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
Power of attorney if the filing is made by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the system issues a 'dossier incomplet' notice, supply the missing items within the statutory 15-day cure period; if registration is refused, correct the defects evidenced in the refusal notice and immediately re-file the electronically revised dossier, avoiding a second greffe fee where the law permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration, Kbis Issuance and INSEE SIREN/SIRET Allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office's jurisdiction; INSEE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation of the dossier, the Greffe registers the SARL in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), issues the official Kbis extract reflecting the corporate form, capital, registered office, and Gérant, and transmits the data to INSEE, which delivers the SIREN, SIC, SIRET, and APE/NAF code (6619) identifiers. Download the Kbis and use it as legal existence proof for corporate bank accounts and licensing applications.
required_dossiers: No additional filing — internal verification checklist of the Kbis against the statuts
Receipt of the Guichet Unique validation
Payment receipt of the registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is delayed beyond the SLA, file a progress inquiry (relance) with the Greffe through the Guichet Unique portal; if the Kbis carries an inaccurate mention, apply to the judge supervising the register for rectification of the RCS entry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance, Banking Activation and Regulatory Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ACPR, ORIAS, the depository and current-account bank, and the corporate tax authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the definitive operating bank account by presenting the Kbis and release the blocked capital; update the beneficial-ownership register if founders change; adopt internal governance instruments (mandates, approval of authorized signatories, procurement of third-party liability and professional indemnity insurance); appoint the statutory auditor if the size thresholds of Article L.823-1 C. com. are exceeded or if imposed by ACPR; and file the initial tax and social declarations, notably the declaration of company existence and the election of corporate tax domicile.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
Final executed statuts
Appointment deed of the Gérant
Bank attestation of unfreezing of the deposit
Declaration of beneficial owners filed with the Guichet Unique
ACPR preliminary information form for the payment-institution license application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACPR does not acknowledge receipt of the preliminary file, send a formal reminder and request a meeting with the ACPR Digital Finance and Innovation Division; if ORIAS registration is required for any payment-distribution activity, rectify the application within 15 days of the ORIAS refusal notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) — Banque de France; Visa Europe and Mastercard Europe as card-scheme network authorizers; ORIAS for mandatory intermediaries
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Agrément d'Établissement de Paiement (Payment Institution Authorisation) pursuant to Articles L.522-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code transposing Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2), covering the issuing of payment instruments (corporate virtual cards) and the execution of payment transactions; separate card-scheme membership approval (Visa Direct / Mastercard Network) is mandatory for full live operation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique et de la Cohésion des Territoires / DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based activity not listed under the ICPE (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) or IOTA water regime (Code de l'Environnement, Articles L.122-1 and L.511-1). No full environmental impact assessment or prior registration is required; only a non-ICPE compliance attestation and waste-reporting enrolment with ADEME are necessary.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or combustion emissions are generated. The registered office must comply with: (i) local municipal wastewater discharge and sanitation rules; (ii) EU Waste Framework Directive 2008/98/EC and Décret n°2021-321 on waste traceability, including WEEE recycling of IT and card-processing hardware via approved eco-organisms; (iii) RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU for electronic payment terminals; card manufacturing is outsourced to ISO 14001-certified suppliers contractually bound to meet REACH and RoHS substance limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety compliance: issuance of the ERP/Code du travail fire certificate for office premises open to staff, including the building owner's fire-load attestation and evacuation plan. Structural clearance: landlord's floor-load capacity attestation and post-fit-out structural inspection if vaults or heavy racks are installed. Occupational clearance: completion of the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP), workplace medical fitness visits for employees, and mandatory access-control and secure-area clearances for the card-spending control and monitoring room.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) of the French Ministry of Economy and Finance; central taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr; non-resident and special-licence unit: Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE), 10 Rue du Centre, 93160 Noisy-le-Grand; corporate and customs identifiers are issued via the Guichet Unique operated by INPI (RCS registry) and French Customs (Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL: (1) incorporate through the Guichet Unique INPI electronic procedure, obtain statutory SIREN/SIRET and RCS registration certificate (extrait Kbis); (2) DGFiP automatically attributes the TVA-intracommunautaire VAT ID (format: FR + 2-digit control key + 9-digit SIREN) and the EORI number (FR + SIREN) for customs declarations; (3) for foreign entities without a French permanent establishment, register directly with SIEE using the CE form or via the EU One-Stop-Shop portal; (4) virtual-card issuers with a high-risk licence must also present the SIREN, VAT ID, and EORI certificates to the ACPR/Banque de France licensing file and card-network due diligence (Mastercard/Visa).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — France is a unitary state with a single national corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) and no sub-national corporate tax. A SARL is by default subject to IS at the 25% standard rate, with a reduced 15% rate on the first €42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs with turnover below €10 million; this fits the tax classification model for a commercial B2B virtual-card issuing fintech.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no US-style check-the-box election. Relevant statutory mechanisms include: (1) Article 239 bis AA CGI — 'SARL de famille' pass-through election at the partners'/members' level, restricted to family-held companies meeting shareholding conditions; (2) Article 223 A CGI — tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) for French groups; (3) Article 145 CGI — mother-daughter participation regime for dividend income; (4) VAT options: régime réel normal, régime simplifié de l'encaissement (cash-basis accounting), or option for the franchise regime where eligible; (5) ATAD 2 anti-hybrid declarations under Articles 202 A ter and 212 bis CGI for cross-border hybrid structures involving French credit-card investment vehicles.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Franchise en base de TVA (Article 293 B CGI): SME exemption thresholds of €85,800 annual turnover for goods and €34,400 for services, revalued to €91,900 and €36,800 as of 2025 (tolerance bands €101,000 and €39,100); a separate €10,000 EU OSS threshold applies to cross-border distance sales from other Member States; non-resident suppliers are subject to indefinite VAT registration without exemption; a virtual-card issuer supplying exempt financial services will typically hold registration for recovery and B2B reporting purposes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured e-invoicing and e-reporting under Article 289 bis CGI (French 'Facturation électronique' reform): Phase 1 from 1 September 2026 — all VAT-registered companies must receive PEPPOL-compliant structured e-invoices (Factur-X hybrid, UBL or CII), and large and mid-cap companies must issue them; Phase 2 from 1 September 2027 — SMEs and microenterprises must issue; invoices are transmitted via certified PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) platforms or the free public portal (PPF) connected to Chorus Pro, with mandatory electronic reporting of B2B, B2C, and transaction data to DGFiP; France does not apply a fully real-time digital stamping clearance as in Italy or Poland, but the PPF architecture enforces peer-to-peer clearance, structural data validation, and near-real-time reporting for payment and financial-transaction flows.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For this B2B virtual-card issuer, the applicable mechanism is not classic goods-export 0% rating but: (a) tangible goods exports — 0% VAT under Article 262 CGI with mandatory proof of physical export from the EU; (b) cross-border intra-Community supplies — 0% under Article 262 ter CGI, conditional on the customer's valid EU VAT ID and movement evidence; (c) financial services such as card issuing, payment processing, and interchange settlement — VAT-exempt without input credit under Article 261 C 3° CGI when performed in France, and outside the French VAT scope for B2B services to non-French taxable persons under the place-of-supply rule of Article 259-1 CGI, triggering reverse charge in the customer's country; services to non-EU non-taxable clients fall outside French territorial VAT; consequently, the entity claims 'exemption/outside scope' rather than 'export zero-rating' for its core fee and interchange revenue.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU) and, for intra-EU transports, the EXS declaration or Export Summary Declaration
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR road consignment note proving physical removal from the EU
Commercial invoice and the virtual-card service contract showing the B2B nature and place of supply
Inward Remittance Certificate (attestation de rapatriement des devises) and bank statements demonstrating FX repatriation to the French treasury account
Payment network settlement statements (Mastercard/Visa) evidencing interchange and scheme fee flows for the exported card services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP tax audits (vérification de comptabilité) apply heightened scrutiny to zero-rating claims and to VAT-exempt financial supplies, particularly against sham-export and artificial routing structures; documentation must be retained for 10 years (Article L.102 B of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales). Penalties: Article 1729 CGI imposes a 40% penalty for underdeclaration in bad faith (mauvaise foi) and 80% for manifestly abusive fraud (manœuvres frauduleuses); Article 1727 CGI adds late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; reclaims and VAT credits are clawed back with interest, and criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGIDP may result in fines up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years, in addition to publication of sanctions and possible suspension of the financial-services licence by the ACPR.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) in coordination with the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR) and the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. France maintains no exchange controls on capital movements, but requires statistical reporting to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments purposes. Profit remittance is unrestricted, subject to standard corporate tax withholding (if applicable) and compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) regulations. Non-resident investors may freely repatriate dividends, interest, and liquidation proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds. Exporters may retain foreign currency in designated accounts, but must report all cross-border transactions exceeding €12,500 to the Banque de France for statistical and balance-of-payments monitoring. No minimum conversion ratio is mandated.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Cross-border Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) licensed in other EU/EEA states may passport into France under the PSD2 regime. However, for a corporate virtual card issuer, the entity itself must hold an EMI or payment institution license from the ACPR or a passporting license. Using an EMI as a banking partner is viable for operational accounts, but capital escrow accounts typically require a full credit institution to ensure safeguarding and regulatory compliance. Legal constraints include adherence to ACPR AML/CFT requirements and the need for a local agent or branch if passporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For high-risk entities such as a virtual card issuer, French banks generally require physical presence of the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and senior management for an in-person KYC interview. Remote onboarding is possible for lower-risk profiles, but for this business scope, most tier-1 banks mandate at least one in-person meeting at the bank's premises or a notarized verification. Some banks accept video interviews with enhanced due diligence, but physical presence remains the default for initial onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business model (virtual card issuance) flagged for potential money laundering, fraud, or terrorist financing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide ACPR license or proof of application; comprehensive AML/CFT policy manual; transaction monitoring system description; risk assessment report; board resolution approving AML compliance; appointment of a compliance officer with relevant experience; audited financial statements; business plan detailing customer due diligence procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ownership structure or non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart with full UBO identification (name, address, nationality, ownership percentage); notarized copies of passports; proof of source of funds for capital injection; bank references from existing financial institutions; legal opinion on the corporate structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of physical presence or substance in France
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for registered office; employment contracts for local staff (compliance, operations); utility bills; tax registration certificate; evidence of local management decision-making.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected sanctions exposure or PEP (Politically Exposed Person) involvement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results from reputable databases (e.g., OFAC, EU, UN); PEP status declaration and enhanced due diligence file; independent audit of screening processes; legal attestation of no sanctions links.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols require SWIFT MT103 with purpose code '1100' (Direct Investment) or '1101' (Equity Capital) for capital contributions. The remitter must provide supporting documentation including board resolution approving the injection, share subscription agreement, and proof of source of funds. The receiving bank will verify the purpose code and may request additional KYC documents. For EU-origin transfers, SEPA transfers are acceptable for amounts below €100,000, but SWIFT is recommended for larger sums. All transfers must be reported to the Banque de France if exceeding €12,500.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements include SWIFT MT103 for direct payments, and Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for documentary trade. For virtual card issuer operations, outbound disbursements to merchants are typically executed via card network rails (Mastercard/Visa) but for non-card trade payments, SWIFT MT103 is standard. Use of MT202 for interbank transfers is also permissible. All outbound payments must comply with EU sanctions and AML regulations, and be reported for balance-of-payments statistics.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forwards (deliverable) in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and other major pairs
Currency swaps (cross-currency interest rate swaps) for long-term exposure
FX options (vanilla and exotic) for hedging contingent exposures

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for currencies with convertibility restrictions, but since EUR is fully convertible, NDFs are not typically used; however, they may be allowed for exotic currencies if the counterparty is a licensed bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax declaration ('liasse fiscale'): Forms 2065-SD, 2050-series schedules, corporate tax computation and statutory financial statements annexed; filed electronically through a DGFiP-approved EDI partner.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques) - French Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second working day after 1 May for calendar year-ends (typically 2-6 May); within 3 months of the fiscal year close for non-calendar year-ends.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% (40% if filed after formal notice) plus 0.2% monthly late-payment interest under CGI Art. 1727-1728; automatic tax assessment (taxation d'office) and joint liability of the managing officers for repeated default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit ('dépôt des comptes annuels') at the commercial registry: balance sheet, income statement, notes, management review, draft profit appropriation and the shareholders' approval minutes, filed for publication in the RCS.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) of the registered office jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholder approval of the accounts, and in any event by 7 months of the fiscal year-end (Art. L.232-23 Code de commerce); a 31-Dec year-end requires approval by 30 June and deposit by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice by registry, court injunction with daily penalties (astreinte), criminal fine up to EUR 9,000 for managing officers (Art. L.241-7 C. com.), denial of dividend distribution, and administrative strike-off (radiation from RCS) for uncured two-year default.
